1.notes: Single claim on the base guard; candidate.

claims.quote: The new ensure_connection() guard permanently blocks reconnecting on any backend after a connection is closed inside an outermost atomic block entered with autocommit off.
claims.notes: Reproduced offline on SQLite with autocommit off: flags stay True, connection None, every later query raises the new ProgrammingError. No family; awaits ruling.

2.notes: Single claim; equivalent to the canonical stale test-database pool claim. The worker sentence is a further manifestation.

claims.quote: The pool is cached per alias with connect kwargs frozen at creation and is never invalidated when settings_dict changes, so create_test_db() and setup_worker_connection() keep using the old database.
claims.notes: Early query creates the pool for the original database; create_test_db's close() and NAME switch leave it, so migrate, tests and flush run on the original database.
evidence: clone-work/chk.py pool unchanged after NAME switch

3.notes: Single claim on fork inheritance of an opened pool; separate mechanism from item 2, novel.

claims.quote: The class-level _connection_pools dict is inherited across fork(), so child processes reuse an already-opened pool whose worker threads are gone and whose sockets are shared with the parent.
claims.notes: Plausible from source (class-level dict, no post-fork reset, open() no-op on an open pool) but the review itself did not exercise it and no server is available here.
evidence: No PostgreSQL server provisioned; fork scenario not run

4.notes: Single claim on slots held by threads that never close.

claims.quote: A checked-out connection is only returned to the pool by an explicit close(), so threads that end without closing their Django connection permanently consume a pool slot.
claims.notes: putconn happens only in _close(); a bounded pool makes unclosed connections in self-managed threads costlier than before. Closing connections in such threads is already the caller's responsibility; pool accounting after garbage collection was inferred, not run. A doc note would help; below threshold.

5.notes: Single claim on connection errors surfacing as PoolTimeout.

claims.quote: Connection and configure failures no longer surface in pool mode; callers get a generic PoolTimeout after the pool timeout (default 30s).
claims.notes: Reproduced with an unreachable port and timeout 2: OperationalError caused by PoolTimeout after 2.0s, real error only logged. This is psycopg_pool's documented checkout behaviour for an opt-in feature and the timeout is configurable; operational advice below threshold.
evidence: clone-work/chk2.py: 2.0s, OperationalError from PoolTimeout, 'Connection refused' only on the pool logger

6.notes: Single claim on missing session reset.

claims.quote: _close() returns the connection to the pool with no session reset
claims.notes: True by source; leaked user session state is ordinary pooling behaviour and already applies to persistent connections, which also configure only at connect. Hardening/doc advice below threshold.

7.notes: Single claim on the bound configure callback with a remedy.

claims.quote: The shared pool's configure callback is a bound method of whichever DatabaseWrapper first created the pool
claims.notes: Capture confirmed; divergent role/time zone needs a copy() with different OPTIONS on the same alias, a test-only pattern. Design advice below threshold; does not state the role re-entry.

8.notes: Single claim on the reserved-keyword collision; candidate.

claims.quote: User pool options are splatted alongside the hard-coded kwargs/open/configure/check arguments, so any documented ConnectionPool option with one of those names raises TypeError.
claims.notes: Reproduced offline; documented dict pass-through fails for these keys with a raw TypeError. Awaiting ruling.

9.notes: Single claim on close_pool with a pop() remedy.

claims.quote: close_pool() goes through the lazily-creating `pool` property twice and then does an unconditional del, so it builds a pool just to close it and can raise KeyError under concurrency.
claims.notes: Build-to-close confirmed; KeyError race not demonstrated; test-signal/teardown path. Below threshold.

new_candidates.claim: The new guard in BaseDatabaseWrapper.ensure_connection permanently prevents reconnecting on any backend after a connection is closed inside an atomic block entered with autocommit off, because Atomic.__exit__ leaves in_atomic_block and closed_in_transaction True and close() early-returns.
new_candidates.evidence: clone/django/db/backends/base/base.py:271-279 (guard added by the change); clone/django/db/transaction.py:301-313; clone-work/chk.py on file SQLite with AUTOCOMMIT=False: state (None, True, True), ProgrammingError 'Cannot open a new connection in an atomic block.' on every later query even after close(). clone-work/chk2.py shows default autocommit is unaffected.
new_candidates.limits: Shown only on SQLite offline; the base revision was not executed side by side (guard absence taken from the diff). Does not show how often autocommit-off deployments close or lose a connection inside atomic.
new_candidates.relevance: Could add a new causal family for a backend-agnostic regression; affects items in five reviews, two of which (blind-492fbb item 8, blind-5e59cb item 9) state the mechanism without the autocommit-off trigger.
new_candidates.confidence: high for the mechanism; medium for materiality
new_candidates.would_settle: A human ruling on whether the autocommit-off regression meets the correction threshold, and whether wording lacking the autocommit-off trigger identifies it.
